recorded.outcome:q-display-name-limit: Page: "A `String` is a sequence of UTF-16 `char` values, and every index counts them. A character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, such as most emoji, takes two: a surrogate pair." The example "Hi \uD83D\uDC4B" prints `5 4` (length 5, 4 code points), so one non-BMP emoji adds 2 to length(). The stem says all six emoji are outside the BMP, so length() is 12 > 10 and the name is rejected, for the reason the key gives.

recorded.outcome:q-pasted-blank: Page: "`strip()` (Java 11) and `isBlank()` use `Character.isWhitespace`. It accepts the em space but excludes the no-break space U+00A0". The output row `U+00A0  trim: false strip: false` shows strip() leaving U+00A0. Also: "`isBlank()` returns `false` for a field holding only U+00A0, so a required-field check accepts it." So strip() on a lone U+00A0 leaves it, isEmpty() is false, and the field counts as filled in.

recorded.outcome:q-total-due: Page: "In a replacement, `$4` means \"group 4 of the match\"". The example `template.replaceAll("\\{amount\\}", "$42.50")` (a pattern with no groups) prints `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: No group 4`, and the page adds "A price with a dollar sign threw". By the same rule, "$7.00" refers to group 7, which the pattern lacks, so it throws IndexOutOfBoundsException. This is an analogy from $4 to $7, but the rule is stated in general terms.

recorded.pass:q-display-name-limit:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-display-name-limit:b: The result (rejects) matches the key, but the reason is wrong. Page: "A `String` is a sequence of UTF-16 `char` values, and every index counts them". length() counts UTF-16 units, not UTF-8 bytes. The example also shows length 5 for "Hi " plus one emoji, which fits 2 units per emoji and not 4 bytes (that would give 7). Refuted.

recorded.pass:q-display-name-limit:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-display-name-limit:c: Page output `5 4`: length() (5) differs from the code point count (4), so it does not count what the user sees. Also: "Where the limit is what a user sees, `java.text.BreakIterator.getCharacterInstance()` finds the boundaries." Refuted.

recorded.outcome:q-display-name-limit:d: Page: a character outside the BMP "takes two: a surrogate pair", and the Design Note says Java 5 added code points "through surrogate pairs instead of changing `char`". So one char per emoji is false. Refuted.
